title: verdict: holds
repro: read diff; login route checks is_active after ensurePetitionLogin (src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts:41-56); emailSchema lower-cases and trims so the email match is exact; no DELETE FROM users anywhere in src, so the INSERT branch cannot re-create a removed account

title: broken: a whole 12-digit Aadhaar is still stored when its groups are split by a full-width hyphen or stop, an en dash, a non-breaking hyphen, a minus sign, a comma, an underscore, or more than 3 whitespace characters (a line split with indentation, CRLF plus a blank line)
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.p5probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass5/probes/reviewer  (clean.review.test.ts, 'no whole Aadhaar is stored')
evidence: maskAadhaar('2345–6789–0123') returns it unchanged; cleanReading keeps '２３４５－６７８９－０１２３' whole in subject, name and full_text (stored in petitions.reading and, after approval, in complaints/petitions); the same for 'Aadhaar: 2345\n     6789\n     0123'. 10 of 10 separator cases fail
cause: SEP is a fixed list [\s./-, zero-width] with at most 3 between groups. The fix claims full-width digits but not the full-width hyphen U+FF0D / full stop U+FF0E that the same keyboard types; Word and OCR produce U+2013/U+2011/U+2212. A mask built on separators needs 'any non-digit, non-letter run up to N' or a digit-only pass (strip non-digits, find 12-digit runs, map back)

title: broken: 'a 12+ digit mobile is dropped' is not true for a 12-digit Aadhaar starting 91 written without spaces: 10 of its 12 digits are kept as the mobile
repro: same probe file, "'a 12+ digit mobile is dropped and marked'"
evidence: cleanReading({mobile:'912345678901'}).mobile === '2345678901' (marked unsure, but kept and shown on the check screen; fileSchema accepts any 10 digits so it can be filed)
cause: the length test runs on tenDigits(m), which has already stripped a leading 91 from any 12-digit run; only the 4-4-4 shape test looks at the raw text. A 91-stripped result that is not a mobile ([6-9]...) should be dropped too

title: broken: 'Zone 6, Ward Seven' (or 'Ward VII') is read as ward 6, the zone, with no mark
repro: same probe file, 'the ward is one number with clear edges'
evidence: wardNumber('Zone 6 / Ward VII') === 6; cleanReading ward 6 with no 'ward' in unsure_fields
cause: when the word 'ward' is present but no digits follow it, the function falls back to 'the only number', which is another number (the zone). If 'ward' is named and not followed by a number, the answer should be unclear/marked

title: broken: a time written with a dot before the date gives a confident wrong date: '9.10 am, 20.3.2026' is read as 09.10.2020; '10.30 a.m. 15.03.2026' loses the date
repro: same probe file, "'the first real date wins'"
evidence: normalDate('9.10 am, 20.3.2026') === '09.10.2020' (a past date, so not marked); normalDate('10.30 a.m. 15.03.2026') === null
cause: the fix guards only ':' times ((?<![\d:]) and [^\d:]); the Indian '9.10 a.m.' form has a dot, so the time's hour.minute pairs with the date's day as a 2-digit year, and matchAll then skips past the real date

title: broken (code path): the officer's date box is stored with no mask, so an Aadhaar typed there is kept whole in petitions.petition_date
repro: POST /api/manu/petitions/<id> {action:'file', fields:{..., date:'2345 6789 0123'}} as the desk; read petitions.petition_date
evidence: code: every other typed field goes through maskAadhaar before the writes (lines 217-220, 230, 237) but f.date is written as typed; '2345 6789 0123' is 14 chars and passes the schema
cause: the 'mask every field the officer typed' pass missed the date field (it is free text, not validated as a date)

title: verdict: holds for the claims (claim-then-send, closing retry reads current status, off on non-saving AWS copy and SMS_MODE=off); two new faults below
repro: read diff; the AWS store is one SQLite file per PC (lib/aws/store.ts header) so the UPDATE claim is atomic across processes there too; first sends use INSERT IGNORE on the unique (complaint_code, kind)
evidence: only one claimant gets affectedRows=1; smsMode() is checked before both send paths

title: a retry interrupted between its claim and its result (server restart, killed process, the 'failed' UPDATE itself throwing) leaves the row 'sending' for ever: it is never tried again and the desk shows 'failed'
where: src/lib/manu/sms.ts:131-133 (sweep selects status IN ('failed','waiting') only) and 148-153 (claim sets 'sending')
repro: code path: set a petition_sms row to status='sending', attempts=1, tried_at an hour ago; run retryFailedSms(): the SELECT never returns it, nothing else resets 'sending'
evidence: no code moves 'sending' back to 'failed'; before the fix an interrupted retry stayed 'failed' and was retried
cause: the claim has no lease: treat 'sending' older than a few minutes as failed in the sweep's WHERE (status = 'sending' AND tried_at <= due)

title: closing messages that wait while their complaint is open are skipped with 'continue' but stay in the sweep's first 20 rows: once 20 exist, no newer failed SMS is ever retried
where: src/lib/manu/sms.ts:131-145 (ORDER BY s.id LIMIT 20, then continue without changing the row)
repro: code path: 20 petition_sms rows kind='closed', status='failed', attempts<4, whose complaints are back 'In Progress', plus one newer failed 'received' row: the newer row is never selected
evidence: the waiting rows keep status, attempts and tried_at, so they match the same SELECT every 15 minutes
cause: the 'wait while open' rule should be in the SQL (join complaints and skip open ones) or push tried_at forward, not a loop continue after LIMIT

title: verdict: holds (anonymous complaints are out of the only online lookup); the 404 check is weak: any existing petition id, including long-filed ones, still runs the lookup with any mobile from the request body
repro: as the desk: POST /api/manu/petitions/1 {action:'repeats', mobile:'<any>', ...} where petition 1 is filed weeks ago
evidence: getPetition(id) only tests that the row exists; the mobile is not tied to the petition's reading. Results carry codes and titles, not names (judgeRepeats drops name/address)
cause: 'on the desk' is not checked (status needs_check/read_failed); acceptable since only the desk login reaches it

title: verdict: holds; officer-console routes refuse the desk only because ref_departments has no COL-PET row (incidental, not an explicit check)
where: src/lib/assistant/access.ts:33; src/lib/officer/guard.ts:46-57 (officerSession needs deptProfile(code) from ref_departments with action_owner=1)
repro: swept src/app/api for every guard: collectorSession (role collector), assistantSession (now refuses COL-PET), officerSession (deptProfile('COL-PET') is null: not in district_intel/output/curated ref_departments), getActiveSessions in complaints/media (desk has department_id NULL), officer/photos and rehearsal/photo (owner dept must equal COL-PET), manu/* (desk's own)
evidence: no route found that gives the desk data outside the Manu Desk and its account pages
cause: if a COL-PET row is ever added to ref_departments with action_owner=1, officerSession lets the desk into the whole officer console; an explicit PETITION_DEPT refusal in officerSession would make it independent of data
